newsitem.title: USA: SAFECO sees deal adding to net after 1998.
newsitem.headline: SAFECO sees deal adding to net after 1998.

text.p: SAFECO Corp said Monday it expects the acquisition of American States Financial Corp to contribute to its earnings after 1998.
SAFECO said today it had agreed to acquire American States for $2.8 billion. Lincoln National Corp, which owns 83.3 percent of American States's shares, said it would support the deal.

SAFECO President Boh Dickey, speaking to Reuters in a telephone interview, said the deal would have a "neutral" impact on 1998 earnings. SAFECO expects the deal to close by the end of September, he said.
Dickey said he expects the deal to increase earnings in 1999 by about seven percent and to increase earnings in 2000 by about 11 percent.

Although the acquisition will significantly expand SAFECO's operations outside its West Coast base, the company still expects to achieve some cost savings through the elimination of some overlapping functions, he said.
SAFECO expects to reduce the combined workforce of about 10,000 by about five percent over the next several years, Dickey said.
He said SAFECO hopes to accomplish much of that staff reduction through attrition.
SAFECO expects to achieve after-tax cost savings of about $22 million in 1998, $42.4 million in 1999, $57.3 million in 2000, and $67.7 million in 2001, Dickey said.
The company plans to issue $700 million in common stock and use $600 million in internal funds to help finance the deal. SAFECO will use preferred stock and bank debt to pay for the balance, he said.
The company said it plans to use $2.5 billion in interim financing from BankAmerica Corp.
Although SAFECO is paying a healthy 23 percent premium over American States's closing stock price on Friday, the company is not concerned that it is overpaying, Dickey said.
He said the company will receive a tax savings with a present value of about $4-$5 a share for the writeoff of goodwill, which essentially brings the price for SAFECO down to $42-$43 a share.
The deal will contribute to SAFECO's earnings after 1998 and bring important geographic and product diversification, he said.
Most other property-casualty deals have consisted of distressed sellers; in this transaction, American States is a healthy, well-run company deserving of a somewhat higher premium, Dickey said.
SAFECO said it was represented by Smith Barney.
Lincoln National said in March it had hired Goldman Sachs to explore a possible sale of American States.
